newsitem.title: FRANCE: France urges Alcatel-Lagardere bid for Thomson-CSF.
newsitem.headline: France urges Alcatel-Lagardere bid for Thomson-CSF.

text.p: The French government is urging Alcatel Alsthom and Lagardere to bury the hatchet and bid jointly for defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF.

"The government isn't imposing a marriage on them but this is what it has asked the chairmen of these companies to do," said a government official, confirming reports that Prime Minister Alain Juppe was looking for a joint bid.
Alcatel and Lagardere have been at loggerheads since the government's first attempt last year to privatise the Thomson SA group.
"We need to reinforce the defence electronics industry ...especially when you consider the huge concentration taking place across the Atlantic," the official said, speaking on condition of anonymity.
He said the government planned to use the privatisation of its 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF initially as an opportunity to group together the main French defence players.
"During this first phase, the French companies can indicate who their allies are within the European industry," he said. But he said the plan was to forge European links at a later stage.
The French government is not open, he said, to a purely foreign offer, even from a European company such as Britain's GEC Plc which already has ties to both Lagardere and Alcatel.
"A 100 percent GEC, and purely GEC, offer doesn't correspond to the French industry restructuring we envisage," the official said.

Joint Alcatel-Lagardere control of Thomson-CSF "will only work if they're willing, which is why the government isn't imposing this condition. It's up to them to see if they're capable of making a joint offer," said the official.

A spokesman for Alcatel declined to comment on the possibility of a joint bid but recalled chairman Serge Tchuruk's recent remarks that it would be unwise to have too many "contradictory interests" represented on Thomson-CSF's board.

Tchuruk told the newspaper Le Monde two weeks ago that he did not feel "entrenched or aggressive" toward Lagardere but that a controlling shareholder was needed at Thomson-CSF to carry out a restructuring of the French electronics industry.
"Lagardere hasn't said so, but they feel the same way," said analyst Bernard Angeniol at brokerage Schelcher Prince.
"It would be lovely if everyone could get along nicely, but that will be hard," he said.
Lagardere officials were not available for comment.
